DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are forty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet. Electronic calculators may be used.

Lysosomes contain many different hydrolytic enzymes that may act within cells (intracellular enzymes) or outside cells (extracellular enzymes). Which process must occur in order for lysosomal enzymes to act outside the cell?

options.A: active transport

questions.questionText: The diagram shows an enzyme, its substrate and an enzyme/substrate complex. enzyme substrate enzyme/substrate complex Which statement explains how the substrate is able to enter the active site of the enzyme?

options.A: Contact between the substrate and the enzyme causes a change in the enzyme shape.
options.B: The shape of the active site and the shape of the substrate are complementary.
options.C: The substrate within the active site forms hydrogen bonds with amino acids.
options.D: When the enzyme/substrate complex forms, the tertiary structure of the enzyme changes.

questions.questionText: What could be used to calculate the rate of an enzyme-catalysed reaction?
Cholesterol is an integral component of the cell surface membrane. Which statement about cholesterol is correct?

options.A: It allows ions to pass freely through the cell surface membrane.
options.B: It has a hydrophobic head and a hydrophilic tail.
options.C: It helps to regulate the fluidity of the cell surface membrane.
options.D: It reduces the mechanical stability of the phospholipid bilayer.

questions.questionText: Which type of bond in phospholipids has a role in increasing the fluidity of cell surface membranes?

options.A: C—C

questions.questionText: Which of these substances can pass directly through cell surface membranes without using a carrier protein or a channel protein?
Companion cells use ATP to move hydrogen ions out of the cell and co-transporter proteins to allow hydrogen ions to return with sucrose molecules. Which two processes are involved in this movement?

options.A: active transport and diffusion

questions.questionText: A culture of bacteria was allowed to reproduce using nucleotides containing the heavy isotope of nitrogen (15N). After several generations, all of the bacterial DNA molecules contained heavy nitrogen. DNA was extracted from a sample of the culture, mixed with caesium chloride solution and spun at high speed in a centrifuge. In this process, DNA molecules of different masses separate into bands at different positions in the centrifuge tube. The heavier the DNA molecules, the closer to the bottom of the centrifuge tube that a band forms. The diagram shows the position of the DNA molecules containing heavy nitrogen in the centrifuge tube. K L M The culture of bacteria was then allowed to reproduce using nucleotides containing the light isotope of nitrogen (14N). DNA samples were taken and separated by centrifugation after the bacteria had divided once and again after the bacteria had divided twice. In which positions would the DNA be found after the cells had divided once and after the cells had divided twice? after dividing once after dividing twice

options.A: half at K and half at L quarter at K, quarter at M and half at L
options.B: half at K and half at M quarter at K, quarter at M and half at L
options.C: all at L half at K and half at L
options.D: all at M half at L and half at M

What will increase the rate of transpiration?
Which properties of water are important for transport in xylem?
Which statement about the blood flow in the cardiac cycle is correct?

options.A: Blood flows into the aorta through the semilunar valve due to contraction of the right ventricle.
options.B: Blood flows into the left atrium through the pulmonary artery when the wall of the left atrium relaxes.
options.C: Blood flows into the right atrium through the vena cava when the wall of the right atrium relaxes.
options.D: Blood flows into the right ventricle through the semilunar valve due to contraction of the right atrium.

questions.questionText: Which of these statements about the formation of haemoglobinic acid are correct?
What can combine with the haem group of a haemoglobin molecule?
Which factors would help a person to adjust from living at a low altitude to living at a high altitude?
Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) includes bronchitis and emphysema. Which symptom is specific to emphysema?

options.A: excess mucus secretion by the goblet cells
options.C: loss of elasticity of the alveolar walls
options.D: thickening of the smooth muscle of the bronchi

questions.questionText: What identifies the structures present in a bronchus? cartilage cilia A C
Which of these terms can be used to describe the role of mosquitoes in the transmission of malaria?
Bacteria that infect skin wounds can become resistant to the antibiotic commonly used to kill them. Which statement explains how these bacteria could become resistant to the antibiotic?

options.A: Exposure to the antibiotic causes a change in the bacterial cell wall, preventing the antibiotic from working.
options.B: Other bacteria that normally protect the skin against infection are killed by the antibiotic, allowing the infectious bacteria to survive.
options.C: Random mutations in DNA allow some of the bacteria to survive in the presence of the antibiotic.
options.D: The antibiotic causes the bacterial DNA to mutate, allowing the bacteria to survive in the presence of the antibiotic.

questions.questionText: Some children are born with severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID). Children with this inherited disease do not normally have any T-lymphocytes and suffer from many infectious diseases. How may these children be cured from SCID?

options.A: transfusion of antibodies

questions.questionText: The hybridoma method is used for the production of monoclonal antibodies. Which two types of cell are used in this method?

options.A: stem cell and B-lymphocyte

questions.questionText: A vaccine is used to create artificial active immunity. After being given a vaccine, it will take a period of time before a person develops long-term immunity against the disease. Which statement about this period of time explains this delay?

options.A: No memory cells have been produced from B-lymphocytes.
options.B: No plasma cells have been produced from B-lymphocytes.
options.C: The primary immune response has not produced enough antibodies.
